units.source_heading: Imatinib for gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST): treatment and checks
units.source_text: The usual National Cancer Control Programme starting dose is 400 mg by mouth every day with food. For progression in advanced disease, a specialist may consider 800 mg daily as 400 mg twice daily. Adjuvant treatment after resection is described as up to 3 years in this National Cancer Control Programme document; your specialist confirms duration using current risk and evidence. The 28-day graphic is a reference view, not a treatment break or fixed course.

units.source_text: For unresectable or metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST), imatinib aims to control disease and symptoms. After removal of higher-risk GIST, adjuvant treatment aims to reduce the chance of recurrence. These are different treatment goals and must be clearly recorded.
units.reason: The complete source statement occurs in current consolidated narrative under approved acronym normalization.

units.source_text: Ask / act: Call oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, very little urine, severe rash or vomiting that prevents drinking. Follow your hospital’s temperature and contact instructions. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizures: call 112/999. Rapid weight gain, new swelling, breathlessness, severe rash, jaundice, fever or significant bleeding needs prompt assessment.

units.source_text: Confirm whether treatment is for advanced disease or after surgery, and the exact daily dose. Review all prescribed, over-the-counter and herbal products; avoid grapefruit and St John’s wort. Never increase the dose after a scan or a missed dose without the team.
units.reason: The complete source statement occurs in current consolidated narrative under approved acronym normalization.

units.source_text: Take the prescribed dose with a meal and a large glass of water. Take doses consistently. If swallowing is difficult, ask the pharmacy about the exact supplied product before changing how it is taken.
units.reason: The complete source statement occurs in current consolidated narrative under approved acronym normalization.

units.source_text: If you miss an imatinib dose, take it when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose; then skip it and return to the usual schedule. Never double a dose. Ask the team what to do after vomiting; do not take a replacement dose without advice.
units.reason: The complete source statement occurs in current consolidated narrative under approved acronym normalization.

units.source_text: Keep tablets or capsules in their supplied packaging, away from children, and follow the pharmacy storage instructions. Do not share medicines or alter the dose yourself. Ask the pharmacy before crushing, opening or dispersing a medicine; formulation-specific instructions differ. Return unused treatment to the pharmacy.
units.reason: The complete source statement occurs in current consolidated narrative under approved acronym normalization.

units.source_text: Full blood count every 2 weeks for the first 12 weeks, then monthly. Kidney and liver tests monthly. Review weight, swelling, breathlessness, rash, bowel symptoms and interactions; additional tests depend on findings. Imaging follows the individual disease or recurrence-monitoring plan.
units.reason: The complete source statement occurs in current consolidated narrative under approved acronym normalization.

units.source_text: National Cancer Control Programme 00244 uses regorafenib 160 mg by mouth once daily on days 1–21 of a 28-day cycle, followed by 7 days off. The team may reduce the dose in 40 mg steps or interrupt treatment; do not change the dose or restart independently.

units.source_text: Regorafenib aims to control gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) after progression on, or intolerance to, both imatinib and sunitinib. Your team explains the likely benefit, uncertainty, alternatives and the monitoring needed for your circumstances.

units.source_text: Ask / act: Call oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, very little urine, severe rash or vomiting that prevents drinking. Follow your hospital’s temperature and contact instructions. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizures: call 112/999. Severe abdominal pain, significant bleeding, chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache, confusion, yellow eyes or dark urine requires urgent assessment.

units.source_text: Confirm that both prior imatinib and sunitinib treatments have been reviewed. Reconcile all prescription, non-prescription and herbal products, including warfarin and the liver enzyme cytochrome P450 3A4 interactions; avoid grapefruit and St John’s wort. Agree liver-test and blood-pressure appointments before starting.

units.source_text: Swallow tablets whole with water after a light, low-fat meal, at a consistent time. Your pharmacy supplies the written food and dose instructions for the product you receive.
units.reason: The complete source statement occurs in current consolidated narrative under approved acronym normalization.

units.source_text: Take a missed dose when remembered on the same day. Do not take two doses on one day. Do not take extra tablets after vomiting; contact the team if vomiting continues.
units.reason: The complete source statement occurs in current consolidated narrative under approved acronym normalization.

units.source_text: Keep tablets or capsules in their supplied packaging, away from children, and follow the pharmacy storage instructions. Do not share medicines or alter the dose yourself. Ask the pharmacy before crushing, opening or dispersing a medicine; formulation-specific instructions differ. Return unused treatment to the pharmacy.
units.reason: The complete source statement occurs in current consolidated narrative under approved acronym normalization.

units.source_text: Liver tests at least every 2 weeks for the first 2 months, then monthly or more often as indicated. Blood pressure weekly for the first 6 weeks, then before each cycle and as needed. Blood count/kidney tests regularly; thyroid/pancreatic tests and cardiac review when indicated. Monitor international normalised ratio (warfarin clotting test) closely with warfarin.
